predictions.title: Router-only LoRA lands as default MoE fine-tuning recipe by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 8 router-only LoRA convergence — the Unsloth + Hugging Face joint arxiv preprint reporting 71-78% recovery of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy at 8-13% of training-step time and 11-16% of peak VRAM across a four-model ablation (Qwen3.6-Max, Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX, Kimi K2.6), Unsloth's same-day production recipes for Llama 4 Behemoth single-node tuning, Kimi K2.6 on a 96GB workstation, and Mixtral 8x22B for sovereign-cloud customers, the parallel DeepMind preprint on router-aware advantage decomposition closing the long-context Reinforcement Learning stability gap that previously kept router-only mode out of ultra-long-context training, and Cerebras's CS-4 engineering-sample announcement explicitly naming Mixture-of-Experts router-only training plus ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning as the target workload — together force the router-only adaptation mode out of the Unsloth-specific category and into the default fine-tuning recipe shipped by every major training stack inside the same calendar window. The structural force is that the four-model ablation gives downstream framework maintainers a published parity baseline they can target without re-running the search, and the DeepMind stability proof removes the last operational reason to keep training all expert weights for a router-shaped objective. The most likely shape is a router-only adapter type added as a first-class option in Hugging Face PEFT, NVIDIA NeMo, Microsoft DeepSpeed, and Meta's torchtune, with default recipe templates targeting at least the Llama, Qwen, and Mixtral families; sovereign-cloud customers and on-prem RTX 6000 Ada workstation tier buyers adopt it first because the VRAM reduction is the only path to single-node tuning of Behemoth-class MoE models. Bear case is a competing scaling-law preprint showing the accuracy gap widens past 200B parameters and forcing a hybrid mode; absent that, Q4 2026 lands router-only as the documented default across the cohort.

reasoning.because: Unsloth + HF arxiv ablation: 71-78% accuracy at 11-16% VRAM across four MoE models.
reasoning.given: DeepMind router-aware advantage proof closes long-context RL gap; CS-4 targets router-only workload.
reasoning.so_that: HF PEFT, NeMo, DeepSpeed, torchtune ship router-only adapters as first-class default MoE fine-tuning recipe.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; sovereign-cloud + workstation-tier buyers adopt first.
reasoning.plain_language: Researchers showed you can fine-tune giant Mixture-of-Experts models by training just the router, and major training tools will copy that shortcut.

predictions.summary: A May 8 Unsloth + Hugging Face arxiv preprint shows router-only LoRA recovers 71-78% accuracy at 11-16% VRAM across four MoE models. DeepMind ships a long-context stability proof; Cerebras CS-4 targets the workload. By Q4 2026 router-only adapters ship as default MoE fine-tuning recipe.

predictions.title: AI-accelerator vendors lock mid-quarter forward-supply 8-K cadence by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the May 8 dual filing — Nvidia's 8-K disclosing that Vera Rubin sampling has reached production-volume customer commitments for nine of the top ten hyperscaler and neocloud accounts with H1 2027 NVL576 rack revenue backlog-covered through Q3 2027 at the current Blackwell B200 ~1,000 NVL72 rack/week production cadence, plus AMD's CFO 8-K supplement to the May 5 print confirming a 6.2GW total Helios + MI450 H2 2026 commitment book across Microsoft Azure, Oracle, OpenAI's standing 1GW first data center, Crusoe, CoreWeave, Lambda, plus a previously-undisclosed 0.8GW Tencent Cloud commitment for Asia-Pacific deployment — combined with the same-day Cerebras CS-4 engineering-sample announcement plus disclosed OpenAI $10B multi-year second-data-center coverage, the post-Cerebras-IPO public-market multiple anchored under disclosed AI-accelerator revenue, and the SEC Corp Fin sample comment letter cycle pressing the Mag-7 cohort on capital-allocation attribution and customer-concentration footnotes, force AI-accelerator vendors (Nvidia, AMD, Cerebras, plus the SambaNova / Groq / Tenstorrent S-1 cohort behind them) to adopt a structured mid-quarter forward-supply 8-K pre-print cadence as the standard disclosure shape, separate from earnings releases. The forcing function is that once two duopoly issuers ship dual same-day forward-supply 8-Ks with named-customer commitment GW figures, sell-side coverage and SEC Corp Fin staff treat the format as the operative template for forward-visibility disclosure — silence between earnings becomes the anomaly rather than the norm. The most likely shape is a recurring mid-quarter 8-K naming production cadence, customer-by-customer GW or rack-count commitments, geographic-region splits where material, and forward-revenue-coverage windows. Bear case is SEC Corp Fin issuing Reg FD selective-disclosure guidance that pushes the cadence back into earnings-call-only territory; absent that, by Q4 2026 the Q3 print cycle lands with at least two prior pre-announcement 8-Ks per accelerator issuer.

reasoning.because: Nvidia + AMD ship same-day May 8 forward-supply 8-Ks naming GW + customer-by-customer commitments.
reasoning.given: Cerebras IPO multiple + SEC Corp Fin sample letter + Mag-7 capex-vs-revenue ROI gap pressure cohort.
reasoning.so_that: AI-accelerator vendors adopt a recurring mid-quarter forward-supply 8-K pre-print cadence as standard disclosure.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; >=2 pre-announcement 8-Ks per issuer ahead of the Q3 print cycle.
reasoning.plain_language: Nvidia and AMD both filed surprise customer-update reports on the same day, so chip vendors will keep filing them between earnings.

predictions.summary: Nvidia + AMD May 8 dual 8-Ks disclose Vera Rubin nine-of-ten hyperscaler commitments and a 6.2GW Helios + MI450 book including 0.8GW Tencent Cloud. By Q4 2026 AI-accelerator vendors lock a recurring mid-quarter forward-supply 8-K cadence as standard disclosure.

predictions.title: AISI cyber-eval reciprocity locks in as allied procurement gate by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the May 8 reciprocity-perimeter expansion — Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI publishing a parallel memorandum-of-cooperation accepting AISI-administered TLO-range cyber-evaluation runs as satisfying their respective frontier-model voluntary-disclosure regimes (120-day placement window) inside 24 hours of the May 7 EU-UK joint memorandum, with Canada CCCS and Australia ASD ACSC pre-committing to mirror language by Q3 2026 and the Mythos + GPT-5.5 results cited as the operational threshold — combined with HM Treasury's same-day extension of the public-sector LLM-coding-assistant procurement pause to a 30-day formal review naming Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini Code Assist, and Microsoft GitHub Copilot for Government tenants in a temporarily-suspended-vendors annex pending Mythos-class capability disclosure under the AI Procurement Common Standard, force the AISI-administered cyber-evaluation regime to consolidate as the operative gating criterion for sovereign + allied public-sector AI procurement across at least six jurisdictions before Q3 2026 closes. The forcing function is that once Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI lift the EU-UK template into the Indo-Pacific within one news cycle and a Five Eyes member (UK) names the Big-4 frontier-lab + hyperscaler-coding-assistant cohort by vendor in a procurement-freeze annex, the absence of a parallel US recognition pathway converts the FMRB executive order draft from a domestic-disclosure question into a market-access question for US-based labs. The most likely shape is a six-or-seven-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter (UK + EU + Singapore + Japan + Canada + Australia, with New Zealand or South Korea as the seventh) treating an AISI-administered cyber-eval pass as a per-tenant Mythos-class capability disclosure, paired with a UK + EU + at-least-one-Indo-Pacific allied named-vendor procurement-gate annex tied to that pass. Bear case is that the FMRB EO ships first with §708-equivalent reciprocal recognition language and short-circuits the multilateral path; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the perimeter as the operative procurement gate.

reasoning.because: Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI publish reciprocity MoC May 8 within 24 hours of EU-UK joint memorandum.
reasoning.given: HM Treasury 30-day freeze names Big-4 frontier-lab + coding-assistant vendors.
reasoning.so_that: AISI cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter consolidates as the gating criterion for allied sovereign AI procurement.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; six-or-seven jurisdictions; second named-vendor annex.
reasoning.plain_language: Britain, the EU, Singapore, and Japan agreed to share AI safety tests; allies will copy the rule for buying AI.

predictions.summary: Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI sign a cyber-eval reciprocity MoC within 24 hours of the EU-UK joint memorandum, while HM Treasury extends a 30-day procurement freeze naming Big-4 frontier-lab vendors. By Q3 2026 AISI cyber-eval reciprocity locks in as the allied-procurement gate.
